name: Geological CO2 storage in saline aquifers
applications: permanent storage of captured CO2 from industry, power and gas processing
principle: Captured CO2 is compressed to a dense phase, piped or shipped to an injection site and injected through wells into a porous rock formation filled with salt water, below an impermeable caprock. The CO2 is trapped under the seal, dissolves in the brine and, over long periods, can mineralise. Injection raises reservoir pressure, so capacity is limited by the pressure that the rock and caprock can tolerate; operators manage it with well placement, completion design and sometimes brine production. Monitoring wells and surveys track the plume.

performance.basis: thick carbonate aquifer; high-rate brine production; multi-depth injection alone gave 13%, both together 44% with storage efficiency 0.58%

name: Physical solvent gas treating (Selexol, Rectisol, Purisol)
applications: separate H2S and CO2 streams for sulfur recovery and CO2 storage or EOR
principle: Acid gases dissolve in an organic solvent in proportion to their partial pressure, with no chemical reaction. name: Chemical EOR (polymer and surfactant flooding)
applications: extra oil from mature waterflooded fields
principle: Chemicals are added to injection water to recover oil that waterflooding leaves behind. Polymers such as hydrolyzed polyacrylamide (HPAM) raise the viscosity of the injected water so it sweeps the reservoir more evenly and water breaks through later. Polymer and surfactant performance depends on salinity, temperature, adsorption on the rock and injectivity, so candidates are screened in the laboratory and by core flooding before a field pilot.

name: Well plug and abandonment (cement plugs, rig-based)
applications: permanent closure of wells at end of life
decommissioning of platforms and subsea wells
principle: A well that is no longer needed is permanently sealed so that formation fluids cannot reach the surface. Barriers, usually cement plugs set across producing zones, above the liner top and near the surface, are placed from a rig after the well is killed and equipment is removed. Standards differ in the barriers they require, for example Indonesia's SNI 13-6910-2002 and Norway's NORSOK D-010, and the choice drives cost. Newer methods such as through-tubing abandonment aim to avoid pulling the completion.
